text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 13 in history.
1093 - Malcolm III of Scotland, son of King Duncan, died during his fifth attempt to invade England at Alnwick, Northumberland.
1312 - Edward III of England born. He also assumed the title king of France in 1340, triggering the Hundred Years' War between the two countries.
1567 - Maurice of Nassau and Prince of Orange born. He was appointed chief executive of Holland and took charge of the republic's army in its struggle for independence from Spain.
1782 - Esaias Tegner, one of Sweden's great poets best known for his "Fritiofs saga", born.
1850 - Scottish novelist Robert Louis Stevenson, author of "Treasure Island", "Kidnapped" and "The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde", born
1868 - Italian composer Gioacchino Rossini, famed for his operatic comedies such as "The Barber of Seville" as well as such grand operas as "William Tell", died.
1907 - The first helicopter to achieve free flight carrying a man, designed by Paul Cornu, rose six feet (two metres) above the ground at Lisieux, France.
1935 - George Carey, 103rd Archbishop of Canterbury, born. He succeeded Robert Runcie in April, 1991.

1940 - Walt Disney's film "Fantasia", which depicted various pieces of music set to cartoon and starred Leopold Stokowski and Mickey Mouse, opened in New York. It was the first film to use stereophonic sound.
1945 - General Charles De Gaulle was elected president of the French Provisional Government with the vote of all 555 deputies.
1956 - The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that segregation of the races on public buses was unconstitutional.
1970 - In Syria, Hafez al-Assad seized power in a bloodless military coup.
1973 - The "cod war" between Britain and Iceland subsided when the Icelandic parliament approved terms of settlement.
1973 - A state of emergency was declared in Britain after power workers and coal miners began industrial action.

1974 - Film star and director Vittorio De Sica died. He was at the forefront of the realist movement in cinema with "Bicycle Thieves" and "Umberto D." and also directed "Garden of the Finzi Continis".
1980 - The U.S. spacecraft Voyager I sent back the first close-up pictures of the planet Saturn.
1982 - U.S. President Ronald Reagan lifted sanctions against European firms supplying components for a Soviet gas pipeline.
1985 - In Colombia, the Nevado del Ruiz volcano erupted, killing an estimated 25,000 people.
1989 - The Pakistani cabinet resigned, giving Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto a free hand to form a new government.
1992 - A group of retired military officers made an unsuccessful attempt to assassinate Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and overthrow the government.
1994 - Swedes voted by 52.2 percent in a referendum to join the European Union.
1995 - A bomb attack on a U.S.-run military centre in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killed seven people, five of them Americans.
1995 - Israel began pulling troops out of the West Bank city of Jenin to end 28 years of occupation.
